jamie: Quick follow-up — I addressed the inline assertion change from earlier review. Swapped the strict assert for a deterministic, non-blocking pattern and added a unit that reproduces the race. PTAL when you have a sec. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1234
sasha: Thanks — quick q: is the new test still using time.sleep? would prefer event signaling so it isn't flaky. can you paste the test snippet here?
jamie: pasted snippet below, i replaced sleep with an Event and updated the mock to be deterministic:
```python
def test_handle_race_condition(monkeypatch, threading_event):
    # simulate delayed kv release and make it deterministic via event
    monkeypatch.setattr(kv, "release", delayed_release_event)
    client.trigger_release()
    threading_event.set()
    resp = client.handle(...)
    assert_resp_ok(resp)
```
jamie: local run: `pytest tests/test_kv.py::test_handle_race_condition -q` -> passed 10/10 locally, no sleeps left
ci-bot: CI build 5123 — tests passed (1 flaky test flagged) :white_check_mark: https://ci.internal/build/5123
dan: LGTM from infra side. one request: add a short changelog note that explains why we moved to a non-blocking assert (so future debuggers know it's intentional)
jamie: added a one-line changelog entry and a comment in the test explaining determinism. PTAL @sasha @dan
sasha: left one tiny nit: rename `delayed_release_event` -> `delayed_release_signaler` for clarity. otherwise :+1:
jamie: renamed, squashed the commits and pushed. Want me to merge once canary slot completes (we have an opening at 21:00 PST)?
dan: fine with merge after a successful canary — I can take the canary at 21:00 and watch for regressions
jamie: re-requesting review after squash — PTAL when free
sasha: LGTM. merge after canary passes.
